sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most repeated failure point is getting the deposit back out of escrow. Pace Morby warns that when an agent submits commission instructions, the Gator has to make sure title knows the EMD is lent and expects a return, and on the Texas deal Stewart Title's escrow officer said policy requires signed authorization even if it is within the contract [qbBAO0ozP-0 @ 00:14:14]. The pivot was having the seller pre-sign Stewart's EMD release form, held with a sticky note, because Texas and Utah are mutual release states and the Section seven clause only works 90% of the time [qbBAO0ozP-0 @ 00:19:17]. On a $250,000 deposit, the attorney required notice to the seller before cancellation, so the team sent UPS overnight letters and posted timestamped notices on the door to recover the money, and the lesson Pace drew is that cancellation processes differ by title company [T5jtdYhM6tQ @ 00:09:18]. Abdiel Garcia Rodriguez builds the guardrail into intake: funding only inside the inspection period with at least 48 hours remaining, plus a written understanding from title or escrow, and a signed mutual release in the file [min0RpX32uc @ 00:05:30]. Skip any one of those steps and the money can end up paid to the assignor instead of the lender.

Borrower risk scales with the tier. Crushing REI calls EMD lending an unsecured loan aimed mostly at broke newbies, since large wholesalers likely keep $1,000 on hand, and reports that a buyer on one of their own assigned deals borrowed EMD and the deal still fell through because the buyer had no funding [jDAbeOWsBX4 @ 00:09:06]. Pace Morby labels second-lien renovation money, Gator 3.0, the most dangerous tier, using the example of a contractor named Juan taking a $60,000 deposit [aIHVhFGaNAw @ 00:24:36]. Roger and Diane Oquist lived it: an Oklahoma loan split three ways ended with about $1,000 lost after a non-judicial foreclosure that cost roughly $6,000 and took a couple of months, because with a deed-in-lieu all the liens follow the property while foreclosure clears them [S9WonQBbHG8 @ 00:32:39]. Their fix afterward was a maximum of one or two deals per borrower, lower ARVs, and weekly reports plus a timeline instead of monthly payments, after admitting they were not getting weekly or bi-weekly progress reports at the time [S9WonQBbHG8 @ 00:40:17]. A second $25,000 deal with the same borrower was recovered, but another borrower ran and turned out to be carrying a separate lien.

The economics checks cut both ways. Pace Morby's case for the chunk model is that 10% on $5,000 is only $500 a year, against $10,000 earned on a $5,000 probate deal, but building to that level takes about a year [7yVZPbb03bc @ 00:13:41]. Late fees are a real line item: Pace had $65,000 in first position for 11 days returning $30,000 with a $500-per-day late fee that had accrued about $7,000, and a Mississippi loan of $60,000 ran 35 days late at $150 a day for $5,250 in late fees and $15,300 total [S9WonQBbHG8 @ 00:44:44]. Fraud is the other check: on deals over $1 million, Pace says to physically visit the office or send a FaceTime proxy, with the California and Utah Attorneys General slated to present on fraud including fake title companies, and to charge $200 to $1,000 upfront because that fee also filters out bad deals [T5jtdYhM6tQ @ 00:10:08]. Tom McKay's audit is that roughly 90% of the success stories show no completed deals, and Mike says 'can fund EMD' posts draw no engagement [cvQX0jcvIFc @ 00:12:20]. Run the numbers against deal flow, too: the rule of thumb on the Oquist call is underwrite 10, you get one.

callout.title: Do not wire a dollar until these four checks clear
callout.body: Every loss and near-loss reported by the Gators traces back to escrow return mechanics, borrower concentration, or skipping the upfront filter [Pace Morby — T5jtdYhM6tQ @ 00:09:18].

chapters.question_prompt: How do I become the transactional lender myself, and how do I build and scale a profitable funding business?
chapters.title: Becoming the Transactional Lender
chapters.subtitle: Loan-type fundamentals for new funders, same-day double close programs, interim financing for agent-wholesaler deals, funding students and title-company referrals, lead targeting and fixes, the three reasons funding businesses fail, and the 138-deal blueprint
chapters.executive_summary: Practitioners running transactional desks agree the product is simple: front the full A-to-B purchase price, release it only after the B-to-C buyer's money sits in escrow, and collect the wire back the same day. Pricing clusters at 1 to 2 points on double closes, with Oroton laddering from 2 points down to 1.25 on volume and EZ Real Estate Platform's Pete charging 1% or less, while EMD funders charge 20 to 50% of a refundable deposit. Ryan Schrope reports $3.7M funded in 30 days for about $83K profit and $149K in a single December using other people's capital split 50/50. Disagreements: Clicks Geek runs no underwriting while Mandy Cartahenna underwrites acquisition only; time windows range from under 24 hours to three business days; and Greg pushes '$0' funding baked into a buyer premium against a race to the bottom.

sections.heading: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Every lender working this lane runs the same core trade: a short loan that funds the wholesaler's A-to-B purchase and gets paid off from the B-to-C sale before the day is out. Hard Money Mike lays out the lingo -- A is the seller, B the wholesaler, C the end buyer -- with ownership moving from seller to wholesaler to end buyer and the loan 'paid off in the same day' [i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:01:38]. The control that makes the trade safe is identical from shop to shop. Mike's desk sends documents and the wire the same day but informs title that it will not close or fund until the end buyer's money is there and verified [i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:02:46]. Mandy Cartahenna, a seven-year investor turned funder on Fund My Real Estate Deal, wants the B-to-C funding in escrow first before supporting the A-to-B side, and funds only deals where the money never leaves escrow, which is why no security documents are needed [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:04:47]. Adam Schneider, a Raleigh hard money lender at Oakwood Lending, releases nothing until both sides are signed and C's funds sit in escrow, and underwrites on that security instead of on property valuation [VxkBvKoeA38 @ 00:02:33]. The lender is not betting on the house; the bet is on a wire already parked at title.

The reasons to double close instead of simply assigning the contract line up just as tightly across channels. Hard Money Mike names three: a contract that is non-assignable, end-buyer financing that forbids the transfer, and -- most prominent -- a fee too big to show, such as buying at $100K, selling at $150K and keeping the $50K off the buyer's radar [i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:00:32]. Ryan Schrope's list overlaps almost word for word: hide the profit, work around states that ban assignments, and serve institutional buyers that refuse assigned contracts, with the rule that only wholesalers use the product and A-to-B must close before B-to-C [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:18:05]. The Real Estate Wealth Network host tells of a partner who saw a $50,000 assignment fee, 'flipped out,' and demanded the wholesaler's price, and takes away that you might choose not to assign even when you can [m77TLPPF8KA @ 00:01:24]. Greg on EZ Real Estate Platform goes further, warning that assignment confusion is the 'birthplace of a lawsuit,' which pushes big-spread operators toward two clean, separate closings [KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:20:42]. The consensus floor is equally clear: the product earns its keep only when the spread is wide enough to swallow a second set of closing costs and still leave the wholesaler paid.

The borrower-side checklist is short, and the operators say so bluntly. Clicks Geek's funder asks for identity documentation, entity documents to confirm who is signing, both purchase-and-sale contracts and an introduction to the title company, then will 'take the bull by the horns' and put up 100% of the cash, closing costs included [cgY-PRTdUB4 @ 00:01:25]. Pete on EZ Real Estate Platform runs no credit check and no underwriting; the A-to-B and B-to-C contracts are the whole file, and LLCs or personal names both work [KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:34:19]. Where the operators tighten up is the end buyer. Adam Schneider at Oakwood Lending says C must be cash or hard money because 'a bank loan won't work' [VxkBvKoeA38 @ 00:01:39]. Pete's end-buyer guidance points the same way: FHA carries about a 90-day seasoning requirement, conventional lenders are '50 50,' and cash, private money or hard money is the preferred exit [KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:32:26]. The baseline prerequisites, stacked together, are two signed contracts, one closer handling both legs, and an end buyer whose money can actually land in escrow the same day. In practice that means the lender's real diligence is on the buyer's money and the closer, not on the wholesaler's resume or the property itself.

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Double-close pricing is quoted in points on the full purchase price, and the shops publish real numbers rather than vague ranges. Ryan Schrope charges 1.5% -- $7,500 on a $500K purchase -- against a market range of 1 to 3%, has the money out for one to two hours on a typical deal, and splits the fee 50/50 with a capital partner for about $3,750 apiece [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:24:45]. OrotonEquities posts a volume ladder that rewards repeat wholesalers: 2 points standard, 1.75 at three-plus deals, 1.5 at six-plus and 1.25 at nine-plus [vtoojcHUwHU @ 00:02:29]. Lex Levinrad prices by geography -- 1% ($800) under $100K in Florida, 1.5% above $100K, and 2 to 2.5% outside Florida, available in all 50 states [aX6Stxr8SfM @ 00:02:08]. Lex then runs the wholesaler's net on the REO example: a $10K spread minus the $800 fee and roughly $2K of closing costs leaves $7,200, split 50/50 in the partnership for $3,600 each [aX6Stxr8SfM @ 00:03:04]. For the lender, the unit economics come from turn speed rather than rate: a point and a half on cash that returns the same afternoon can be redeployed on the next file instead of sitting in a single long-dated loan.

The earnest-money lane runs on completely different math. Ryan Schrope's EMD deals run about 30 days (60 to 90 for commercial), the deposit is typically 1% of price -- $5K on a $500K house -- and the fee is 20 to 50% of the deposit; at 40% that is $2K, with $7K repaid [N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:09:21]. The hard rule is that EMD never leaves escrow and must be the amount listed on the contract, so a non-refundable add-on like a $500 Texas option fee gets rejected [N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:13:05]. Mandy Cartahenna tells wholesalers to line up a funder before contracting because the PSA typically demands the deposit within 24 to 48 hours, and every funder Mandy knows protects the money with a mutual release agreement signed with the seller alongside the PSA [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:08:23]. Chris Bounds runs it as a profit-share JV instead: the deposit must be refundable with a study period, the lender spots $5K for a $1K to $4K return paid at assignment or closing, and the paper is a JV agreement between the two LLCs, a personal guarantee and an irrevocable earnest-money document [FG5mYU_-AVQ @ 00:02:29]. Across all three versions, the funder's protection is the same: a refundable deposit that can be pulled back if the deal dies inside the inspection window.

The business side has its own machinery, and Ryan Schrope teaches it as speed plus systems. A deal submission has to get a response in under 30 minutes, through a website or online form, because the investor usually needs EMD within 24 hours [xdTSPoFABEY @ 00:14:31]. At about 10 leads a day and a $250K average deal, Ryan's stack starts with a website and a CRM and graduates to an AI deal-review tool, automated contracts and a deal portal, with a team running the backend [wjyrMCdmO9g @ 00:09:09]. On lead generation, Ryan tells a coaching client stuck in 'Facebook jail' at nine messages a day that one strategic group post a week beats daily ChatGPT-written posts, and to whiteboard each post's hook, value, authority and predicted respondents before publishing [KQxDCgfJ6VA @ 00:08:19]. Mandy Cartahenna reports no capacity limits at all, funding from own money plus raised capital and stacking deals on about $5M in assets, so the constraint becomes deal flow rather than cash [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:12:12]. The common thread across both shops: capital is the easy part, and the edge is the machinery that answers a submission fast, vets it once, and keeps referral and content pipelines full enough to turn deals down.

callout.title: Insider Pro-Tips From Working Funders
callout.body: Operational habits the funders credit for keeping capital safe and deal flow clean.
items: Close both legs at the same title company at the same time, and get it in writing, signed by title, that the funder's money wires back immediately upon receipt -- typically within 30 minutes [Ryan Schrope — N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:08:38].

Issue proof-of-funds letters for the exact offer amount, never a range, because a range lets the seller push the price up; the letter is free, one page, out within 24 hours and valid 30 days [EZ Real Estate Platform — KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:08:31].
Read EMD requests for context clues: a '90 days' timeline or a '1%' figure in the ask signals something is off with the deal [Ryan Schrope — wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:17:06].

Treat a deal submission as a validating signal, not a money opportunity; Jamie rejected one partner's first five deals and then built that partner into an auto-approved pipeline [Ryan Schrope — 2a2qJD8P3gI @ 00:08:46].

sop_steps.title: Camp at the watering hole
sop_steps.action: Find active wholesalers and buyers where they already gather and borrow those audiences.
sop_steps.detail: Work meetups and Facebook or Skool groups with written posts, borrowing other people's audiences instead of building your own, and aim at active buyers, wholesalers and referral partners rather than inactive newcomers [Ryan Schrope — wjyrMCdmO9g @ 00:04:04].

sop_steps.title: Answer every submission inside 30 minutes
sop_steps.action: Collect both contracts, ID, entity docs and a title introduction through an online form.
sop_steps.detail: Run submissions through a website or online form with a sub-30-minute response target [Ryan Schrope — xdTSPoFABEY @ 00:14:31]; the file is identity documentation, entity documents to identify the signer, both purchase-and-sale contracts and an introduction to title [Clicks Geek — cgY-PRTdUB4 @ 00:01:25].

sop_steps.title: Vet the closer and the capital
sop_steps.action: Confirm the title company and the capital partner's money before any live wire.
sop_steps.detail: Vet the title company for fraud, get written confirmation of the capital partner's funding source and run a dry run [Ryan Schrope — 2a2qJD8P3gI @ 00:15:34]; use an investor-friendly title company so the A-B paperwork never leaks to the end buyer [Fund My Real Estate Deal — yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:22:33].

sop_steps.title: Release against escrow, collect the wire back
sop_steps.action: Wire only when both sides are signed and C's money is in escrow, then track the return.
sop_steps.detail: Release funds only when both sides are signed and the B-C funds sit in escrow [Oakwood Lending — VxkBvKoeA38 @ 00:02:33]; Pete reports the funder's money coming back within about two to three hours [EZ Real Estate Platform — KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:38:24].

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: Pricing is the loudest split on the street. Hard Money Mike quotes roughly a point to a point and a half, which is $1,000 to $1,500 on a $100K transactional loan [i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:03:54]. Ryan Schrope charges 1.5%, or $7,500 on a $500K acquisition, and pegs the going market at 1 to 3% before widening that range to 1 to 5% [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:18:05]. OrotonEquities publishes a volume ladder instead of a flat rate: 2 points standard, 1.75 at three or more deals, 1.5 at six or more, and 1.25 at nine or more [vtoojcHUwHU @ 00:02:29]. Pete at EZ Real Estate Platform undercuts the field at 1% or less, and Greg, speaking alongside Pete, describes the category as a race to the bottom sliding from 2 points to 1 point to 75 basis points [KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:11:47]. Their answer is to stop competing on rate entirely: the 1% fee and roughly $2K of closing costs get rolled into a buyer's premium, so the wholesaler sees funding as effectively free. The operator choice: compete on rate and watch margin compress toward three-quarters of a point, or bundle the fee into the premium the way Pete and Greg do so the end buyer's side absorbs it.

Underwriting depth and the funding window split operators into two camps. Clicks Geek runs a no-friction model: bring two purchase and sale agreements, connect the lender to the title company, and the deal closes with no underwriting and no delays [cgY-PRTdUB4 @ 00:01:58]. Mandy Cartahenna on Fund My Real Estate Deal never underwrites the exit either, but reviews the acquisition side and insists that for a double close or end-buyer EMD the refundable period runs all the way through close of escrow [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:02:38]. The window itself is contested. Ryan Schrope treats transactional money as strictly under 24 hours, describing an average double close as literally money moving from one account to another [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:23:28]. OrotonEquities markets the opposite edge: competitors give 24 hours, while its STF program allows up to three business days for short-sale back-to-backs, returns funds with no charge if the buyer defaults, and still demands a mortgage commitment or proof of funds from the end buyer [vtoojcHUwHU @ 00:01:17]. Cartahenna draws the hard line between the two: one to three days stays transactional, five or more becomes a bridge loan. Pick a lane before you advertise it, because the window you promise dictates whether your capital is a same-day flip or a multi-day exposure.

EMD pricing and the assign-versus-double-close threshold produce two more forks. Ryan Schrope prices earnest money as a percentage of the deposit, charging 40%, or $2K on a $5K EMD, against a market of 20 to 50%, and admits the number sounds a bit crazy until you grasp how niche the product is [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:15:06]. The funder featured on Chris Bounds' channel structures the same capital as a joint venture between LLCs, spotting the earnest money for a negotiated $1K to $4K return paid at assignment or closing, backed by a personal guarantee and an irrevocable earnest-money document [FG5mYU_-AVQ @ 00:01:53]. On when to double close at all, Hard Money Mike draws a conservative line: on a $100K to $105K spread the funding takes out too much of the money, so sell the contract instead [i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:04:22]. Pete at EZ Real Estate Platform runs a mechanical rule of thumb, double closing anything over $25K and steering $25K to $60K spreads into double closes so neither seller nor buyer backs out of an assignment [KDMCbsw9VKs @ 00:26:24]. Real Estate Wealth Network goes further still, preferring to skip assignment fees even when the contract allows them. As a lender, your pitch to borrowers should match their spread: thin deals assign, fat deals hide behind a double close.

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The closing table is where transactional deals blow up. Mandy Cartahenna on Fund My Real Estate Deal recounts a title company leaking the A-B purchase agreement and a $100K wholesale fee; the wholesaler had to hire an attorney, surrendered $50K of the fee, and the close slipped a full month [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:19:54]. The lesson is blunt: run every double close through an investor-friendly title company. Ryan Schrope flags the timing trap on the lender side: if the A-B closing funds and the B-C closing is not right behind it, you might just end up buying a house cash [N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:06:34]. Splitting the two closings across separate title companies costs more and adds risk, so the best case is same place, same time, with the title company's signed written commitment to wire the money back immediately upon receipt, typically within 30 minutes [N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:08:38]. Adam Schneider at Oakwood Lending adds a state-level wrinkle: North Carolina is an attorney-closing state, so the same attorney must handle both the A-B and B-C sides, and funds release only when both sides are signed and the end buyer's money is sitting in escrow [VxkBvKoeA38 @ 00:02:16]. Any deviation from that sequence turns a one-to-two-hour loan into an unplanned acquisition sitting on the lender's books.

Small-ticket volume is the trap Ryan Schrope paid for personally. Early on, Schrope funded $5K EMDs at roughly 20%, clearing about $1K each, and chased 30 of those a month to hit $25K; tracking collapsed, deals failed, and most of the money was lost [wjyrMCdmO9g @ 00:11:00]. Now a single $1M deal produces the same $25K, which Schrope frames as 25x the return for the same effort. Borrower selection is the second leak. When a brand-new operator cannot carry a deal across the finish line, in Schrope's experience that means they are probably not going to close the deal [wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:13:11], and context clues like a 90-day timeline or a 1% deposit request signal that something is off. The third trap is drifting out of escrow. Schrope stresses that gap funding is the first product that goes outside of escrow, demanding plans A through Z, with returns of 15 to 30% over three to six months and no place for beginners [N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:22:01]. Mandy Cartahenna only funds deals where the funds never leave escrow and lists what gap actually requires: security documents, a transaction coordinator, collateral, and state-law review, all at a higher price [yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:07:04]. If your funds cannot stay in escrow, you are no longer a transactional lender.

Ryan Schrope's coaching hot seats expose the operational bottlenecks that sink funding businesses before money ever moves. Capital partners are the first choke point: vet the title company for fraud, get written confirmation of the funding source, and run a dry run, because money pulled from the stock market sits idle while timelines slip, large wires can require a physical bank-branch visit, as in a Wells Fargo example, and a partner's W-2 job can block a 10 a.m. wire [2a2qJD8P3gI @ 00:15:34]. Pipeline quality is the second: roughly 70% of Tonio's submissions came from brand-new people, and bird-dog style posts attract newbies who are low-quality partners at the start [2a2qJD8P3gI @ 00:07:05]. Channel risk is the third. Tom landed in Facebook jail and was capped at nine messages a day, while group posts drew title companies instead of the intended audience [KQxDCgfJ6VA @ 00:01:13]. The fourth is half-built systems. Schrope warns that a ChatGPT contract is not battle-tested, that lead generation without systems leaves you worse off than doing nothing, and that active investors doing five deals a month need a response in under 30 minutes [xdTSPoFABEY @ 00:11:58]. Sending money is easy; the 90% of work that happens before funding is where lenders fail.

callout.body: Every loss reported by these funders traces back to wiring before the end buyer's money was locked, trusting an unvetted closer, or funding paperwork that was never battle-tested. Clear all four gates on every deal.

chapters.question_prompt: How do private money and hard money lending work, and can lending replace a 9–5 or scale into a company?
chapters.title: Private Money & Hard Money Lending
chapters.subtitle: Becoming a private lender, the three types of lenders and paying them off, 75% ARV fix-and-flip loans, SDIRA co-lending, first-lien positioning, hard money vs. DSCR, private lending vs. transactional funding, JV agreement timing, scaling lending companies and software, and insider tips for getting funded
chapters.executive_summary: Operators from hard money shops to coaching programs converge on one rule: match lender terms to the exit, lock first position, and never let the borrower run the deal without skin in the game. Pace Morby sorts capital into A, B and C lenders with different payoff clocks, while Ryan Dossey asks for 12 months when a project needs three. Pricing clusters at 12% plus 3 points for experienced flippers at SEP Capital, about 10% and 1 point for Gabrial Carter's High Roller borrowers, and 11.5-16% at Invest Away. Transactional funders charge a flat 14% or a small percentage fee for same-day double closes. The split: Toño Flores says private-lending paperwork protection means a legal battle and pushes 30-day transactional money, while Beth Pinkley Johnson maps four lending vehicles trading return against passivity.

sections.heading: 1. The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Pace Morby answers the pay-forever-versus-refinance question with 'all of the above,' then sorts capital by size and clock [UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:00:21]. Lenders writing $25K or less want their money back within six months, while $100K-$300K lenders rarely ask for it inside a year [UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:00:52]. Morby's A bucket is five-year safe money at 8-10%, the B bucket is professionals placing $50K-$250K for one to two years, and the C bucket is other investors who want to watch transactions through Slack, title, the TC and the bookkeeper before leaving within three months to two years; C lenders make up 80% of the book [UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:05:30]. Ryan Dossey's lender arrives at the same rule from the other side: if a project needs three months, ask for 12, with defaults of one year for three-to-four-month flips and two years for holds, refis and repositions [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:05:09]. Beth Pinkley Johnson makes time horizon the second gate for any new lender, steering three-to-six-month money toward DIY loans and longer money toward debt funds [qCwj0Q01AJY @ 00:01:33]. The shared logic is simple: the note term has to outlast the real exit, not the pitch-deck exit, or someone gets forced into a fire sale.

Lien position is the second point of agreement. Venus Venture lays out the sequence: draft a promissory note, record a mortgage or deed of trust, run a title search with lender's title insurance, and record immediately, because the lien must be recorded at or before closing to guarantee priority [qHujP7kjj4Y @ 00:01:38]. Harley Green of Invest Away learned the cost of ignoring that: early 20-25% second-position loans left the firm 'still waiting for that money to come back,' so Invest Away now lends first position only and has never foreclosed [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:17:54]. Vertical Capital draws the same line around earnest money, refusing to lend on EMD at all because it is unsecured and flagging cross-collateralization as a possible workaround, while pricing gap money higher because a second lien means no control plus mechanics' lien exposure [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:09:28]. Gabrial Carter adds the equity side: the firm never lends 100%, because investors need skin in the game, and lenders who do go to 100% carry higher foreclosure and REO rates [tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:08:26]. Across all four, security beats speed; Venus Venture puts it as 'speed matters, but security matters more.'

Practitioners also agree on where lender capital lives and how to keep it. Ryan Dossey's lender says most private lenders are investors who cannot find deals or retirees who want their capital to stay in real estate, and the opener is a single question: have you ever considered becoming a private lender [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:01:52]. Harley Green started Invest Away from a 401k rolled into a self-directed IRA plus proceeds from underperforming rentals, and now co-originates alongside investor IRAs as equal partners with a $50K minimum [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:04:21]. Tiffany High runs meetups where attendees are told to 'bring three friends' with 401ks, and High went five to eight years without using personal money while scaling to 300 flips in year three [9g6lYN-Aei0 @ 00:27:21]. Daniel Paloscio of SEP Capital says a weekly email blast is the majority lead source and referrals drive most of the business [9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:07:51]. Retention is the quiet multiplier: all Dossey did with that lender was pay the money back as agreed, and the best source of new lenders is referrals from existing ones [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:07:02]. A lender treated well becomes the recruiting engine for the next raise.

sections.heading: 2. Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Pricing on the street is tight and tiered. Daniel Paloscio sets SEP Capital's base at 12% and 3 points for experienced fix-and-flip investors, roughly half of volume, while everyone else pays 4-6 points, and a 12% and 6-point loan is one the team says it loves getting [9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:16:20]. Paloscio's argument is that a borrower closing in seven days does not care about one or two points. Gabrial Carter undercuts that market for repeat operators: the High Roller program requires three to four or more deals and a 680+ score, then pays 90% of purchase and 100% of rehab at one point and about 10%, with no appraisal and a 24-48 hour close [tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:18:44]. Harley Green prices Invest Away loans at 11.5-16% on four-to-nine-month terms, with interest reserve or interest-only options and extensions baked in, and drops borrowers to 0% down after three deals [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:06:06]. Hard Money Mike frames the takeout comparison: hard money runs 9.5-12% for under a year, while DSCR runs 6.5-9.5% but lends only 80% of as-is value and funds no rehab [QMbtBhGx9os @ 00:02:58]. The spread between those quotes is what experience buys.

Transactional money runs on a different clock. Vertical Capital splits it into EMD, double-close and gap funding, and says it would lend on double closes 'all day' because the money sits for two to three hours behind escrow and a lender's policy at up to 100% financing, while the double close lets the wholesaler hide the assignment fee [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:12:51]. Its flat-fee product charges 14% with no monthly payments over three to four months: borrow $100K and owe $114K whether the payoff lands on day 1 or day 88, which the operator calls a 'stupid crazy' rate of return [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:14:11]. Toño Flores reports 48 transactional deals this year with zero losses, terms of 30 days typically and 60 at most, and puts risk at about 0.001%, using the money for EMDs, double closings and the stack method [fv1IoI6DQn8 @ 00:03:10]. Fuel My Deal adds the borrower-side math: a same-day double close carries a small percentage fee, so the wholesale spread must cover the cost, and points, slipping timelines and appraisal results are the risks to price in [cqT1jSeQWKo @ 00:00:17]. For EMD sizing, Vertical Capital notes New Orleans deposits run $500-$3K, with fewer than a handful above $2K across 35 wholesales and 40 listings.

Underwriting and servicing mechanics are where the shops differentiate. Gabrial Carter's intake is photos, contract, rehab budget and experience plus a soft credit pull, underwritten in about 24 hours and closed in one to two days, with ARVs held within plus or minus 5% on software that sees tens of thousands of deals a year [tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:05:31]. Draws get a physical inspection the day after a request, and the borrower picks the schedule: quarters, scope items, 50/50, or one completion draw [tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:25:33]. Harley Green lends up to 75% of ARV on reimbursement-based draws and runs AI agents that check rural and flood zones and analyze photos [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:11:33]. Daniel Paloscio, who lends business-purpose against primary residences, requires a notarized commercial-purpose affidavit and a handwritten use-of-funds statement so the plan for every dollar is on paper [9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:23:50]. At scale, LendingWise customer Jeff Fechter runs HouseMax across 45 states with dynamic document lists and dashboards for 35 loan officers, treats credit as the most important factor, and averages an 11.5-day bridge close, with some loans closing in two to three days [uVDb80-WSkw @ 00:03:29].

callout.title: Small moves operators use to squeeze more out of every lead and every dollar
callout.body: Referral pay, wall-card prospecting, charity-routed payoffs and public listings are tactics operators run every week to feed deal flow and clear lender balances.
items: Pay referral partners about 15% of the origination fee, even when they never asked for it; referrals drive most of SEP Capital's business [Hard Money Mastermind — 9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:09:17].

Pull the business cards off brokerage walls and call every realtor; originator Lisa used it to land a $1.5M St. Pete condo loan against an ARV of about $2.6-2.7M [Hard Money Mastermind — 9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:19:07].
Clear lenders with surplus instead of a refinance: Pace Morby donates to a charity that pays off the lenders, holds the notes, and generates a tax deduction [Pace Morby — UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:02:59].
Push borrower exits to the open market: listing to the public reaches 97% of the market versus 3% for a buyers list [Vertical Capital — 5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:14:32].

sop_steps.title: Raise and bucket the capital
sop_steps.action: Recruit idle investor and retiree money, then sort it by size and payoff horizon.
sop_steps.detail: Ask investors who cannot find deals and retirees whether they have ever considered becoming a private lender [Ryan Dossey — UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:01:52], then slot each one into Morby's A, B or C bucket based on amount and how fast they want the money back [Pace Morby — UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:03:32].

sop_steps.title: Take in and underwrite the deal package
sop_steps.action: Collect photos, contract, rehab budget and experience, then pull soft credit.
sop_steps.detail: Carter's shop underwrites the package in about 24 hours and closes in one to two days, cutting leverage about 10% for no experience or a large rehab [Beyond The Deals Podcast — tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:05:31]; check equity and marketability before anything else [Kai Lu — pqyNMc1tJj4 @ 00:01:03].

sop_steps.title: Paper and record the first lien
sop_steps.action: Draft the note, record the mortgage or deed of trust, and insure title.
sop_steps.detail: Run a title search, buy lender's title insurance, record immediately and use staged escrows [Venus Venture — qHujP7kjj4Y @ 00:00:50]; have a lawyer draft the documents as the final step before funding [Kai Lu — pqyNMc1tJj4 @ 00:01:50].

sop_steps.title: Fund draws and manage the payoff
sop_steps.action: Inspect before each draw, then set a clear notice window for repayment.
sop_steps.detail: Physically inspect the day after a draw request on the borrower's chosen schedule [Beyond The Deals Podcast — tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:25:33]; Morby's agreement with lender Yara uses 90 days' notice, after which Morby finds another lender or refinances [Pace Morby — UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:07:22].

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: Leverage is the sharpest split. Gabrial Carter on Beyond The Deals Podcast says flatly, "we never get up to 100%," because the fund wants every investor to have skin in the game. Carter argues that lenders who do go to 100% carry higher foreclosure and REO rates. Even the firm's High Roller tier stops at 90% of purchase and 100% of rehab, and only for borrowers with 3-4 deals and a 680+ score [tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:08:26]. Harley Green on Real Estate Explainer pushes harder: up to 75% of ARV, and borrowers go to 0% down after 3 completed deals with Invest Away [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:12:45]. Vertical Capital will run 100% financing on double closes "all day." The exposure window is 2-3 hours, the funds sit in escrow, and a lender's policy protects the position [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:12:51]. Hard Money Mike frames the market ceiling as 90% of purchase plus 100% of rehab on hard money, against 80% of as-is value with zero rehab money on DSCR [QMbtBhGx9os @ 00:01:11]. The operator read: 100% money exists, but only on same-day transactional windows or after a borrower has stacked a track record. On a first flip, expect leverage to drop about 10%. Carter tells borrowers to read that cut as the lender's verdict that the deal is thin, not as an insult.

The second fault line is which side of the funding game actually protects capital. Toño Flores talked to six private lenders in a single week and heard nothing but horror stories: slow projects, borrowers who go silent, ARVs that came in low, and foreclosures. In each case "paperwork protection" turned into a legal battle. Flores moved the money into transactional funding instead and reports 48 deals in one year with zero losses. Flores pegs the risk at roughly 0.001%, on holds that typically run 30 days and never pass 60 [fv1IoI6DQn8 @ 00:03:10]. Harley Green counters with a longer-hold book: more than $10M funded on 4-9 month fix-and-flip paper and not a single foreclosure [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:12:18]. Inside transactional funding, earnest money is contested ground. Vertical Capital has never lent on an EMD because the money is unsecured until it lands in title escrow, and names cross-collateralization as the only structure that could make it work [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:09:28]. Pace Morby's Gator crowd funds EMDs as a core play, but only behind a JV agreement written "100% of the time" by attorney Shawn St. Clair [9-Vzu27aIq0 @ 00:00:45]. Flores lists EMDs, double closings and the stack method as the working menu. The real split is in the paper, not the product.

Practitioners also diverge on how hands-on a lender should be and how fast to demand money back. Beth Pinkley Johnson lays out four vehicles on a return-versus-passivity curve. DIY lending puts your name on the security instruments and earns interest plus origination fees, often without accreditation. A private debt fund pools capital, pays pro rata per the PPM, and secures you only by an equity stake in the fund entity [qCwj0Q01AJY @ 00:03:42]. Kai Lu's starter answer for someone holding $10K is to skip direct loans and park the money in a fund returning 5-7% [pqyNMc1tJj4 @ 00:02:51]. Pace Morby flips that script for Gators, calling it the biggest rookie mistake to deploy your own money "cuz they're greedy" instead of riding along on Morby's deals for the first 5-10 [pWyy8qqZobI @ 00:00:52]. Repayment expectations split by bucket. Morby's A lenders want 5 years at 8-10%. B professionals with $50K-$250K want 1-2 years. C lenders, 80% of the roster, stay anywhere from 3 months to 2 years while they watch the transactions. Ryan Dossey's lender takes the borrower-side counter-move and asks for 12 months whenever a project needs 3 [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:05:09]. That buys runway the A-B-C bucket system has to manage with 90-day notice clauses and refinances.

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: Lien position is where real money has already been lost. Harley Green says the early Invest Away book took 20-25% second-position loans: "we're still waiting for that money to come back." The shop now lends in first position only [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:17:54]. Vertical Capital spells out why second-lien gap funding bites. The gap lender covers the 20% on top of an 80% first, has no control of the asset, and sits exposed to mechanics' liens. That exposure is the only justification for charging the higher rate [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:18:06]. Venus Venture's checklist for staying senior is mechanical and unforgiving: promissory note, recorded mortgage or deed of trust, title search with lender's title insurance, and a lien recorded at or before closing to lock priority. After that come staged escrows and ongoing monitoring of reporting, insurance and milestones [qHujP7kjj4Y @ 00:01:38]. Paperwork is also a cost line. Pace Morby's JV agreement ran $7K up front at $450 an hour and landed around $12-13K all in. Every transaction since has still needed an addendum. That is why Morby keeps a dozen investor-friendly title companies per state, treats finding professionals as a skill, and cuts bad title companies from the bench [9-Vzu27aIq0 @ 00:01:20].

Term mismatch is the slow-motion trap. Ryan Dossey holds about 12% of a partnership sitting in month 10 of a 12-month note with 45-60 days of runway left. The lender's blunt read is "fire sale it or refinance it," and in hindsight the price should have been cut months ago [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:04:31]. Fuel My Deal lists the same killers for any hard money or DSCR exit: points, slipping timelines, and appraisals that come in short [cqT1jSeQWKo @ 00:01:53]. Vertical Capital warns that once a flip leans on a takeout loan, "all the control lies in the hands of the refinance company." A short note squeezes exactly that pressure point [5a6OhvT6Dcw @ 00:05:09]. Pace Morby runs into the other side of term risk. Lenders at $25K or less want their money back inside 6 months. That pushed Morby to spend the first 30-40 sub-to deals building enough credibility to replace family money. On one deal it meant borrowing $160K two days before Christmas and refinancing it out by January 10 [UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:00:52]. The economics check from Dossey's lender never changes: can the property cash flow as a rental, or at least cover its costs, if the sale never comes?

Scaling breaks operators faster than bad deals do. Tiffany High ran 40 flips, then 165, then 300 across three years. High then watched the closing team shrink from 12 to 1, shut down for 90 days to rebuild, and separately lost $300K on a syndicate deal [9g6lYN-Aei0 @ 00:25:16]. High also reports that 8 of 10 submitted deals are bad, so volume without screening is just exposure. Ryan Dossey flags the compensation trap. Paying 10-15% of gross on a $10K wholesale leaves $8,500-9,000, and if acquisition cost runs near $8,500 the owner is underwater. Comp plans have to load in cost of goods sold, marketing included [UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:03:09]. Daniel Paloscio at SEP Capital admits the founder-as-bottleneck problem: talent rises to the top, "but the problem with that is that I don't have much time to teach everybody." Meanwhile, paid PPC has underperformed badly enough that it will probably stop [9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:33:14]. On the capital side, the Real Estate Explainer host warns that lenders who brag about lending their "own money" often run on credit lines. Beth Pinkley Johnson adds that with direct-lender placements, you have to underwrite the lender directly, not just the deal [1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:03:12].

callout.title: Four Gates Before Any Wire Leaves the Account
callout.body: Every gate below comes from a loss, a near-miss, or a hard rule a named practitioner now enforces after getting burned or watching others get burned.
items: Wire only after a recorded mortgage or deed of trust, a title search and lender's title insurance are in place, with the lien recorded at or before closing [Venus Venture — qHujP7kjj4Y @ 00:01:38].
Refuse 20-25% second-position flip loans; Invest Away is still waiting on early junior-lien money and now lends first position only [Real Estate Explainer — 1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:17:54].
Set the note term at 12 months when the project plan says 3, so a slipping timeline never forces a fire sale [Ryan Dossey — UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:05:09].
Paper every EMD deal with a JV agreement, budgeting roughly $12-13K for the attorney-drafted template [Pace Morby — 9-Vzu27aIq0 @ 00:01:20].

Require photos, contract, rehab budget and an experience summary on every hard money submission, then underwrite in about 24 hours and close in 1-2 days [Beyond The Deals Podcast — tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:05:31].

chapters.question_prompt: Which documents secure a loan or partnership, and what interest-rate and legal limits must lenders respect?
chapters.title: Loan Documents, Security & Usury
chapters.subtitle: Promissory notes, deeds of trust, mortgages and pledges, land contracts, seller-financing notes, the private lender document set, liens and insurance, business loan agreements, usury laws (including California and litigation finance), predatory lending, and real estate joint venture agreements
chapters.executive_summary: Private lenders and JV operators converge on one rule: the promissory note is the IOU, but the recorded deed of trust or mortgage is what lets you take the house. Hard Money Mastermind runs about 80 pages per loan, puts personal guarantees on 98% of deals, and treats the closing instruction letter as the single most important document. The Real Estate Lender pegs recording at $38, the lender title premium near $1,850, and insurance around $2,400 a year. Usury is the kill switch: Lender Link fixes California at a 10% APR cap with points included, Scott Horne pegs Texas at 18% individual and 24% corporate, and fees can turn a six-month loan into 50%. The split comes on JVs: Clint Coons calls JV agreements lawsuit generators, while Molly Tennant teaches them for quick $20,000 closing money.

sections.heading: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Every lender in this lineup splits the paper the same way: the promissory note is the IOU, and it cannot touch the house. Investor Army frames the note as the borrower's promise at 5, 10 or 12 percent for six months to a year, while the deed stays with the investor and the deed of trust is the instrument that lets the lender foreclose [ltZrMvVSfdw @ 00:02:46]. Manuel Angelus of The Real Estate Lender says it bluntly: the note alone cannot reach the property, and an unrecorded lien is a secret between friends, so recording for about $38 is what sets priority, with property taxes still ranking ahead of everyone [Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:02:26]. Jason of Hard Money Bankers, lending since 2007 across 4,000-plus loans, keeps the note unrecorded but insists on holding the original, while the mortgage or deed of trust goes on record [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:03:09]. Angie Diarth of Inland Professional Title runs the same three-document stack on seller-financed closings: the warranty deed passes title, the note sets the terms, and the recorded deed of trust forces the buyer to carry insurance and pay taxes [JExnsYGsNd8 @ 00:01:57]. The operator takeaway is simple: money moves on the note, but leverage lives in the recorded lien.

The second consensus point is that the borrower's personal balance sheet sits behind the collateral. Trevor Calton of Real Estate Finance Academy states that loans are typically made with recourse, and non-recourse only exists if the documents define it; the lender can both sue on the note and foreclose on the mortgage [Z-MpltBp8qA @ 00:00:19]. Jason of Hard Money Mastermind backs that with hard numbers: 98% of the shop's loans carry personal guarantees, and the one exception, self-directed IRA loans, gets underwritten tighter with LTV dropped from 65% to 50% [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:05:23]. William Dolan of Esquire Advice explains why guarantees matter in a blowup: in bankruptcy unsecured creditors get little and 'survives discharge' clauses are unenforceable, but the guarantor stays on the hook, so the guarantor needs a strong balance sheet because retirement funds are hard to reach [hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:05:55]. Even on the JV side, Clint Coons builds the guarantee into the structure, with the gap funder and the operator both signing personal guarantees for the hard money lender, pitching it to a reluctant funder as protection through default notices and real ownership that keeps them committed [6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:04:18]. The pattern across all four: collateral first, a named human signing second.

The third consensus point: usury is measured on the all-in cost, not the note rate, and the paper must be clean enough to enforce and sell. Scott Horne lists the fees that count toward APR, points, origination, processing, appraisal and lender-required surveys, while title closing costs and buyer inspections stay out [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:03:10]. Nema Daghbandan of Geraci Law Firm, speaking on Lender Link, lands in the same place for California: a 10% cap on an APR basis with points and fees included, so a 9.99% note rate is not automatically safe [W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:01:20]. Ayala Law PA warns from a live trial that the combined rate has to stay under the Florida limits, and a lender that blows past them risks being unable to enforce even the principal [0cBnXayz9w4 @ 00:04:24]. On the instrument itself, Damen Capital Fund draws the hardest line in the room: always use a promissory note with a deed of trust or mortgage, never a land contract, because land contracts drag in seller liability, title policy loss, double transfer tax and forced foreclosure after thresholds like 5 years or 20% paid, which is why the fund pays significantly less for them [mrt2bJ7XfNU @ 00:00:21]. Clean paper and honest APR math are the two prerequisites these lenders share.

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Jason's hard money stack runs about 80 pages per loan, and the build order is worth copying. On top of the note and recorded mortgage or deed of trust sit an assignment of rents, the LLC documents and corporate resolution signed by all members, a commercial-purpose affidavit, a construction security agreement, an AML declaration and an ACH authorization; powers of attorney and remote online notaries go on the avoid list [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:09:55]. The document Jason calls most important is the closing instruction letter, three to four pages the title company must sign, because the title company does not represent the lender; the commitment gets verified directly with the insurer, sticking to Chicago, Fidelity, First American or Old Republic, and money wires only after the HUD-1 and the signed letter are in hand [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:11:31]. William Dolan layers on an assignment of contractor agreements and a lender's title policy with riders [hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:02:41]. Manuel Angelus tells lenders to actually read the policy exceptions on a premium of about $1,850, then name themselves mortgagee and loss payee on insurance running about $2,400 a year, and reverify during the loan because vacancy after 30 to 60 days, builder's risk and flood are the gaps that bite [Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:05:58].

The underwriting math is stated in plain dollars. Investor Army's flip runs a $40,000 purchase plus $30,000 of repairs against a $100,000 ARV, with the lender advancing $70,000 and leaning on a 30% leverage position for protection [ltZrMvVSfdw @ 00:00:44]. Manuel Angelus works a bigger deal: $285,000 purchase, $65,000 rehab, $460,000 estimated ARV and a $200,000 loan, which pencils to roughly 70% LTV, about 57% LTC and about 43% of ARV, paying about $1,666.67 a month at 10% interest-only [Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:04:04]. Clint Coons, walking through the JV agreement on Toby Mathis's channel, routes funder money to escrow instead of the investor: $50,000 within 5 days for acquisition, $20,000 within 20 days for rehab and an interest reserve booked at $8,000 even though $800 a month over 8 months computes to $6,400, for $78,000 total secured by a second deed of trust behind Green Turtle LLC [FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:15:41]. Scott Horne then shows how fees wreck the headline rate: a $50,000 fee on a $200,000 six-month loan works out to 50%, and $2,500 charged on $10,000 of 30-day earnest money works out to 300% [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:04:46]. Every one of these operators runs the full-term APR before quoting a rate to anyone.

Usury compliance is engineered, not hoped for. In California, Daghbandan identifies two exits from the 10% cap: a loan arranged by a licensed real estate broker who earned a fee and secured by real property, or a loan made by a California Finance Lender; the exemption is an ongoing requirement, so an unlicensed holder adding rate, points or even an extra $50,000 advance at the same rate on a modification loses it, while a pure 12-month time extension is fine and late charges, default interest and prepayment penalties sit outside usury entirely [W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:02:48]. In Texas, Scott Horne points to the 60-day cure available through a usury savings clause, while warning that borrowers can still sue for up to about 4 years [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:07:09]. On equity-style deals the payout is scripted in advance: Clint Coons's LLC example nets $100,000, returns the funder's $75,000, and splits the remaining $25,000 at $12,500 each [6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:08:35]. The JV agreement waterfall pays sale costs, a first lien capped at $150,000, any other second lien of $20,000 to $30,000, Party A's $78,000 plus $12,000 of Exhibit B additions for $90,000, Party B's receipted costs, then a 50/50 split [FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:19:36].

callout.title: Closing-Table Moves the Lenders Actually Use
callout.body: These are the small execution details the practitioners lean on to keep a lien enforceable, a JV funded on time, and collateral reachable when a deal goes sideways.
items: Never release a wire until the HUD-1 is reviewed and the title company has signed the closing instruction letter, because the title company does not represent the lender [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:17:38]

Keep Wyoming LLCs pre-formed: a Florida LLC was still incomplete on day 6 of a 10-day close, so a Wyoming entity was formed the same day to save the deal [Clint Coons Esq. | Real Estate Asset Protection — 6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:10:22]

Cap any refinance debt the investor can add at around 10% of FMV and take a pledge of the investor's LLC interests as extra collateral [Toby Mathis Esq | Tax Planning & Asset Protection — FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:09:30]

For an LLC-interest pledge, take possession of the certificate, file a UCC-1, make sure the LLC opted into UCC Article 8, and check the operating agreement for stale managers [Esquire Advice — hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:02:58]

sop_steps.title: Lock Down the Borrowing Entity and Signing Authority
sop_steps.action: Pull the borrower's LLC documents, corporate resolution and operating agreement and confirm who can bind the entity.
sop_steps.detail: Jason requires LLC docs and a corporate resolution with all members signing, and refuses powers of attorney and remote online notaries [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:07:02]; William Dolan warns to watch for stale managers still listed in operating agreements [Esquire Advice — hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:04:29].

sop_steps.action: Add points, origination, processing, appraisal and lender-required surveys to interest over the actual term and compare to the cap.
sop_steps.detail: Scott Horne shows a $50,000 fee on a $200,000 six-month loan hitting 50% [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:04:46]; in California the cap is 10% APR unless a licensed broker arranges the loan or a CFL makes it [Lender Link — W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:01:48].

sop_steps.title: Assemble the Stack and Close Through the Instruction Letter
sop_steps.action: Build the note, deed of trust, guarantees, assignment of rents and affidavits, then deliver the closing instruction letter to title.
sop_steps.detail: The roughly 80-page set includes a commercial-purpose affidavit, construction security agreement, AML declaration and ACH authorization, with the title commitment verified directly against Chicago, Fidelity, First American or Old Republic [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:11:31].

sop_steps.title: Record, Insure and Reverify Through Payoff
sop_steps.action: Record the deed of trust, get named mortgagee and loss payee, and recheck coverage gaps during the loan.

sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest split is over the joint venture paper itself. Clint Coons tells investors to skip the 'JV agreement garbage' entirely. In his view a JV agreement 'ensures a lawsuit': a gap funder can wire $20K, walk away with the project $25K short, and the hard money lender forecloses before anyone gets to court [6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:01:36]. The Coons playbook is to pre-form at least three Wyoming single-member LLCs owned by the Corp and make offers through them. Once an offer is accepted, the gap funder and the investor personally become 50/50 members, and both sign personal guarantees for the hard money lender [6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:04:18]. Coons's own walkthrough on the Toby Mathis channel still calls the LLC the best vehicle, but it treats a written JV agreement as the fallback. That agreement is never signed in your own name, because it can be treated as a general partnership. It is armored with escrow funding, a second deed of trust, and a recorded, notarized copy in the property's county [FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:01:57]. Molly Tennant runs the opposite direction for small checks. Her JV agreement covers someone bringing $20,000 to close and getting paid back, or short-term lending for a share of an assignment fee. It is capped at three parties, and past that an LLC becomes the smarter wrapper [TTA8OtC6qJs @ 00:00:56].

Security paper splits along two lines: land contract versus a note plus a recorded lien, and mortgage versus deed of trust. Damen Capital Fund's rule is absolute: always use a promissory note with a deed of trust or mortgage, never a land contract. Land contracts drag in seller liability, double transfer tax, title-clouding memoranda, liens filed by upset buyers, and forced foreclosure after roughly five years or 20% paid [mrt2bJ7XfNU @ 00:00:21]. William Dolan of Esquire Advice frames the choice by state. Mortgage states force judicial foreclosure, while deed of trust states give the trustee a power of sale. When the collateral is stock or LLC interests, the playbook flips to a pledge, possession of the certificate, and a UCC-1, with an Article 8 opt-in and a commercially reasonable sale [hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:01:49]. Angie Diarth at Inland Professional Title adds that a seller-financier can choose judicial or non-judicial foreclosure and take either the property or just the money [JExnsYGsNd8 @ 00:03:40]. Guarantee policy splits too. Jason at Hard Money Mastermind puts personal guarantees on 98% of loans. Self-directed IRA loans are the exception, so the cushion comes from dropping LTV from 65% to 50% instead. Dolan's counterweight is that a guarantor is only worth the balance sheet behind them [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:05:23].

Usury is where the rate math and the jurisdictions refuse to line up. Scott Horne works with Texas caps of 18% for individuals and 24% for corporate entities, and believes Arizona has none. He counts points, origination, processing, appraisal and lender-required surveys toward APR, while excluding title closing costs and buyer inspections [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:00:32]. In California, Nema Daghbandan of Geraci Law Firm says business purpose does not create an exemption. The cap is 10% on an APR basis, so a 9.99% note rate loaded with points is not automatically safe. The escape hatches are a licensed broker arranging a loan secured by real property, or a California Finance Lender making it [W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:01:20]. Daghbandan carves late charges, default interest and prepayment penalties out of the usury math as borrower elections. Ayala Law, by contrast, argued in a live trial that a lender cannot double-charge late fees and default interest at all [0cBnXayz9w4 @ 00:03:04]. TownCenter Partners pushes a separate line for litigation finance. If repayment is contingent on recovery, there is no loan and no usury. Some courts, however, look past the contract language and ask whether the litigant is virtually certain to win [YahUsg3anlA @ 00:01:34].

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The first failure mode is the money partner who stops funding mid-deal. Clint Coons describes a gap funder who wires $20K, leaves the project $25K short, and lets the hard money lender foreclose before a breach suit can even be filed. Time pressure compounds it. A Florida LLC was still incomplete on day 6 of a 10-day close and had to be replaced the same day by a Wyoming LLC, which carries $50 a year in costs [6bibMzU1L3U @ 00:10:04]. The second failure mode is a runaway operator. Coons's walkthrough cites a $400K demolition horror story. The responses are to bar Party B from exceeding the budget by $8K without approval, and to force a listing within 7 days of completion. Price drops are scripted at 8%, then 5% at 60, 90 and 120 days, down to a $490K break-even floor, after which the property converts to a rental [FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:25:12]. Scott Horne flags the structural trap: a JV built only to dodge usury limits is a sham. The funder has to genuinely participate or hold real ownership in the LLC or on the deed [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:08:27]. Molly Tennant adds that breach is pursued separately, so breach disclosures belong in the agreement up front [TTA8OtC6qJs @ 00:01:56].

Closing-table failures are where private lenders lose principal without any borrower default. Jason at Hard Money Mastermind refuses powers of attorney and remote online notaries, and reminds lenders that the title company does not represent them. He verifies the title commitment directly with the insurer. He wires only after the HUD-1 and a signed three-to-four-page closing instruction letter are in hand [bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:17:38]. Manuel Angelus at The Real Estate Lender puts it bluntly: an unrecorded lien is a secret between friends. A $38 recording fee is what sets priority, and property taxes still jump ahead of everyone [Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:02:26]. Angelus also warns that insurance quietly fails mid-loan. Vacancy exclusions kick in at 30 to 60 days, builder's risk may be missing, and flood leaves gaps. The lender has to be named mortgagee and loss payee and must reverify coverage during the term, not just at closing [Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:05:58]. William Dolan of Esquire Advice raises the authority trap. Operating agreements often list stale managers, so the person signing for the borrowing LLC may have no power to bind it. And once bankruptcy hits, unsecured lenders collect little [hy-UeKXcTUA @ 00:04:29].

Rate and default math is the third trap, and it cuts both ways. Ayala Law's live trial involved a $5M balloon loan. Delayed refinancing let 21% default interest accrue daily, and a new lender retroactively assessed default interest on past late payments under a no-waiver clause. The balance swelled to about $6.4M, and the lawsuit itself then blocked the refinance [0cBnXayz9w4 @ 00:03:19]. On the lender side, Nema Daghbandan warns about modifications of California loans by an unlicensed holder. Adding rate or points, or even advancing an extra $50,000 at the same rate, loses the exemption because no licensed party is involved anymore. That turns an exempt loan into usury exposure [W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:04:14]. Scott Horne shows how fees blow up APR. A $50K fee on a $200K six-month loan works out to 50%, and $2,500 on $10K of 30-day earnest money works out to 300%. Texas borrowers can sue for up to about four years for interest, principal, fees and possibly treble damages, even after a 60-day savings-clause cure [XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:06:38]. Quad's Mississippi case shows the borrower's audit: a 33.04% APR against a 14% cap on loans above $5,000 is a 19-point excess [eFyovu8iZIA @ 01:02:26].

callout.title: Stop Signals Before a Dollar Leaves the Account
callout.body: These four checks come straight from the losses, lawsuits and blown exemptions the practitioners lived through. If any one fails, the wire stays home.
items: Wire nothing until the HUD-1 and the signed closing instruction letter are back from title, and reject powers of attorney and remote online notaries [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:17:38].

Recalculate the all-in APR with points, origination, processing, appraisal and lender-required surveys over the actual loan term before quoting a rate [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:03:10].
On California paper, never add rate, points or new advances through an unlicensed modification; a pure time extension is the only safe change [Lender Link — W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:06:32].
Confirm the lender is named mortgagee and loss payee, and reverify vacancy, builder's risk and flood coverage during the loan [The Real Estate Lender — Bp3FsnPecRY @ 00:05:58].

Run the note checklist (principal, rate, maturity, collateral legal description, default, prepayment, acceleration, notarization) and cross-check it against the deed of trust [Gary Pryde — nKwv-ImRqjo @ 00:05:13].

Build the full package: personal guarantee, assignment of rents, LLC resolution signed by all members, commercial-purpose affidavit, AML declaration and ACH authorization [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:05:58].

Route JV funding into escrow in tranches ($50K acquisition, $20K rehab, $8K interest reserve) and record the notarized agreement in the property's county [Toby Mathis Esq | Tax Planning & Asset Protection — FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:12:10].

chapters.question_prompt: When a deal or business needs short-term gap capital beyond transactional funding, how do bridge loans and lines of credit work, and what goes wrong?
chapters.title: Bridge Loans & Lines of Credit
chapters.subtitle: Buy-before-you-sell bridge loans and their alternatives, investor and commercial bridge loans with exit plans, hard money vs. bridge, how bridge loans go wrong, business lines of credit, velocity banking, high-limit business cards, and closing the small-business funding gap
chapters.executive_summary: Bridge lenders, brokers, and loan officers agree that a bridge loan is short-term, equity-sized debt underwritten on the exit, sale or refinance, which lenders ask about before almost anything else. Residential buy-before-you-sell bridges cap at roughly 70% to 80% combined LTV over 6 to 12 months, and one program advances 70% of value at 0% interest for a fee of 2.4% or $9,000, whichever is higher. Investor bridges run 12 to 18 months at 70% to 75% leverage, tiered by deal count and FICO. They are priced at 11% to 12%, or 1 to 3 points plus higher rates. Line-of-credit operators preach building capacity before a crisis and paying interest only on draws. The fault lines are three: whether a HELOC, recast, or sale contingency beats bridge debt nine times out of 10; the 70% versus 80% cap; and whether revolving business credit should ever fund real estate.

sections.title: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: The operators who originate and broker bridge debt agree on one idea that carries the whole product: a bridge loan is a short-term instrument sized on equity and underwritten on the exit. Easy Lending USA frames it as one subtype inside the hard money family. It is sized on the as-is appraisal with no rehab budget, runs 12 to 18 months, and is driven by the exit, whether a sale or a DSCR refinance [GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:01:06]. Michael Daniel Investments says every bridge loan has an exit and the lender asks about it before almost anything else. The same channel warns that both exits, sale and refinance, depend on other people performing [0EcBhBq5U08 @ 00:01:28]. MKK Capital calls the exit plan non-negotiable and ranks it after collateral, asset-type experience, and liquidity in its commercial review order [k0m3lOvAU7U @ 00:01:06]. Zach Smith, the COO interviewed on Rene Nelson's channel, puts it bluntly: "We look at exit first." The shop will even lend on as-stabilized value when the exit math holds [VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:06:13]. The shared read is that collateral and the takeout path carry the file, while borrower income matters less than on a conventional mortgage. Speed is the product being bought, and every speaker prices that speed above long-term debt.

On the residential side, the consumer-facing lenders converge on one use case: buying the next home with a non-contingent offer before the departing residence sells. Jeb Smith, a Coldwell Banker agent in Southern California, says the whole point is to avoid contingent offers, which sellers pass over when multiple bids land. The same agent calls equity "the key component" behind roughly 80% combined LTV [xOBdb3zZB9Y @ 00:01:33]. Ryan Marks of SEI Mortgage caps combined LTV across both homes at 75%. The three triggers on that list are non-contingent offers, relocation, and speed, and the loan comes interest-only with deferred payments over a 6 to 12 month term [d8gbJrywXFE @ 00:01:40]. Steve Ferguson's standard bridge sits as a lien on the departing residence, in second position or first if the home is free and clear, at up to about 70% of value. Fees run higher because the bank has a short window to earn [AGFnuSOGL68 @ 00:01:10]. Tim Talks Real Estate agrees on the 6 to 12 month term and the hot-market, non-contingent fit, while calling bridge debt one of the most expensive short-term loans available [AkHsQo6uSuU @ 00:01:24]. Across all four, the cost buys the removal of the sale contingency, and equity in the departing home decides who gets in.

The line-of-credit operators share a parallel rule: build the capacity before the crisis. Fast Business Lending says you apply when cash flow is strong, not when you're desperate, and lock in a bank line ahead of trouble [-EPbq7NKBZY @ 00:04:00]. Korean Atlanta Mentorship claims 26 lines of credit totaling $494K, including a $280K HELOC, and gives the same advice: get credit before you need it [NgkU4dL1_sU @ 00:04:36]. The business-credit camp adds that lenders judge how the entity is set up, not just the owner. Velocity Channel's presenter CJ says lenders research the company online and that a gmail.com address gets the applicant written off. CJ adds that lenders date the business from the day its bank account opens, regardless of incorporation date [5IAt1l4ev5w @ 00:04:31]. Noelle Randall says approval needs a registered LLC, a business address, a dedicated phone line, and clean personal credit. Randall's summary is that when the business is set up the right way, banks will lend [UkLPuHL4krM @ 00:07:21]. The core mechanic all of them rely on is revolving access: interest runs only on what is drawn, repaid principal refills the line, and unused capacity sits in reserve at no cost. Bridge lenders underwrite the exit; line lenders underwrite credit score, time in business, and monthly revenue.

sections.title: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Steve Ferguson walks through the numbers on his preferred program, which is not a lien at all. It advances up to about 70% of value at 0% interest with no restriction on use. It also keeps the departing residence out of DTI, provided the home is listed within a set period after closing [AGFnuSOGL68 @ 00:02:07]. In the worked example, a $500K home at 70% equals $350K. Subtract $200K owed and $150K remains, which goes down on a $500K purchase, so the new loan is $350K. Any surplus at sale arrives as a separate check [AGFnuSOGL68 @ 00:04:22]. If the home sits unsold for four months, the program takes ownership and covers payments, taxes, insurance, and repairs. The fee is 2.4% or $9,000, whichever is higher. Eligibility is tight: conventional, FHA, VA, or USDA financing; five acres maximum with no exceptions; no subdivisions heavy with new construction; single-family only; good condition; and pretty good credit. Ryan Marks runs the combined-LTV version. A $1M free-and-clear home plus a $2M purchase caps borrowing at $2.25M under the 75% ceiling, with one loan on two properties and 1 to 3 points [d8gbJrywXFE @ 00:01:06]. RJ Baxter's 80% math differs: $500K times 80% is $400K, and subtracting $300K owed nets $100K [XH6IkQFi_8M @ 00:00:31].

Investor bridge pricing runs on experience tiers and seasoning. Easy Lending USA lends 75% to borrowers with two or more deals at FICO 620+, 72.5% with one deal, and 70% to new investors at FICO 650+. Loan sizes run from $115K to $8M, with cash-out around 65% [GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:03:53]. In the worked deal, a $400K duplex closes in 10 days, bridged at 75% for $300K, which leaves roughly $100K plus costs to bring, with a DSCR refinance as the exit. Seasoning decides the basis. Owned more than 12 months, the loan sizes off appraised value; owned less, it sizes off cost basis, so keep every receipt [GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:04:35]. Zach Smith quotes private-money economics from the lender seat. Investors expect 8 to 10%, so rates land at 11 to 12% with no index tie. Interest-only payments run roughly 1% of balance per month, and max LTV is 70 to 75%, constrained by cash flow. Minimum FICO is 540 [VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:43:19]. Terms run 12 months for residential deals and 24 months plus a 24-month extension for commercial ones. Aravision Funding pitches the speed end of the market: closings in 3 to 5 days, interest-only, no prepayment penalties, no credit checks, no upfront fees, and a reply within one business day [4jdvXuchjXo @ 00:01:01].

On lines of credit, Fast Business Lending runs the cleanest math. On a $50K line with a $20K draw, interest applies only to the $20K. A bank line at prime plus margin costs about $583 over six months, while online lenders run $1,800 to $3,488. A "1.55% monthly fee" works out to roughly 31% APR [-EPbq7NKBZY @ 00:02:35]. Online lenders want 6 to 12 months in business and a score around 625; banks want two-plus years and 680+. The harder the underwriting barrier is to pass, the less the money costs. Velocity Channel's setup sequence is website first, then company-domain email at about $40 a month, then an EIN-backed bank account. The claim is that an owned domain moves approvals into five-digit lines of $10K to $50K+ instead of $3K to $5K [5IAt1l4ev5w @ 00:03:22]. Korean Atlanta Mentorship's velocity-banking play moves $137K of card debt onto a 7.5% line and ranks debts by cash-flow index, balance divided by minimum payment, lowest first. The full paycheck then goes into the line [NgkU4dL1_sU @ 00:06:40]. Noelle Randall reports approvals of $25,000, $35,000, or higher right out of the gate on cards like Chase Ink Unlimited, with 0% for 12 months and stacking across multiple Chase cards [UkLPuHL4krM @ 00:06:12].

callout.title: Moves the operators use to cut cost and tighten the file
callout.body: These are small execution details the lenders and loan officers flag. Each one changes the size of the advance, the all-in cost, or how fast the lender says yes.
items: Keep every receipt on properties owned under 12 months, because the bridge sizes off cost basis instead of appraised value until the asset is seasoned [Easy Lending USA — GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:04:35]

Before signing, ask the lender four things: what an extension costs, whether there is a prepayment penalty, how draws are staged, and what exit they expect [Michael Daniel Investments — 0EcBhBq5U08 @ 00:03:02]
